text:
A defect found from outside the team, with a precise reproduction. Please fix it in this run and add a test that fails before the fix.

STEPS (three real processes, NODE_ID a/b/c on ports 4421/4422/4423, PEERS as the README says, CLUSTER_KEY set):
1. All three up. POST /api/kv/colour {value:"green"} on a -> 200, acks 3, version 1.
2. SIGKILL c. POST /api/kv/colour {value:"blue"} on a -> 200, acks 2, version 2. (good so far)
3. SIGKILL b. POST /api/kv/colour {value:"red"} on a -> 503 "1 of 3 acks, need 2". (good)
4. Restart c on the same database file.
5. GET /api/kv/colour on c.

EXPECTED: the committed winner, value "blue" version 2, and repaired: true.
ACTUAL: value "green" version 1, repaired: false. c is behind the committed value and the read did not repair it.

TWO DEFECTS, both required by README clauses 3 and 4:
(a) A refused write clobbers the committed value on the node that attempted it. After step 3, GET /api/state on a lists colour version 3 in uncommitted, but a's row for the key is now the uncommitted red v3 instead of the committed blue v2. A value that never reached a quorum must not displace one that did; keep it aside (that is what uncommitted is for) and keep serving the committed value.
(b) Read repair does not converge in this scenario. A read on a node that is behind must ask the peers, take the highest committed (version, writer), write it locally and answer repaired: true. A peer that is down, or that holds an uncommitted row, must not stop the repair from finding the committed winner on a peer that has it.

Note the existing cluster.test.js 'repair' test passes and does not cover this: it never writes while a node is down, so it never leaves a node behind a node that also holds an uncommitted row. The new test must reproduce the five steps above and fail on the current code.
